correctness.rationale: For n>=5, q=cos(2pi/n)>0, all n+1 vertices survive exactly if the projected apex planar point Q=-h(u_x,u_y)/u_z violates precisely one side-support inequality of the regular base. Each such cell is triangle with vertices (c,+/-s),(d,0), d=c/q; all other support inequalities hold by convexity. Haar normal projects to isotropic planar Cauchy density h/(2pi(h²+|Q|²)^(3/2)). The triangle solid angle gives p_n(h)=n/pi arctan[2s(d-c)h/D_n(h²)] with D_n(x)=(1+q+2x)sqrt(x+d²)+2(cd+x)sqrt(x+1). For G(x)=(a+2x)sqrt(x+t), 2xG_prime-G has strictly positive derivative, so the sum H_n=2xD_prime-D crosses zero exactly once; this is an analytic all-n proof, not a numerical root search. h_6=sqrt(3/5), p_6=6/pi arctan(sqrt2/22); Taylor analysis yields h_n->1/sqrt2 and n² p_n(h_n)->2pi²/(3sqrt3). Independently integrated triangular Cauchy density and rederived solid-angle equality for n=5,6,8; checks are corroborative only.
residual_risks: Collinear projection directions have measure zero; case n<=4 deliberately excluded. Asymptotic correctness relies on analytic Taylor estimate and compact root bracketing, not finite n.
